I learned the following git commands:

- **git add**: This command adds changes in your working directory to the staging area. It prepares the changes to be committed. For example, `git add .` adds all changes in the current directory and its subdirectories.

- **git commit**: This command records the changes in the staging area to the repository. It creates a new commit with a message describing the changes. For example, `git commit -m "Add new feature"` creates a commit with the message "Add new feature".

- **git push**: This command uploads the local repository content to a remote repository. It sends the committed changes to the remote server. For example, `git push origin main` pushes the changes from the local main branch to the remote main branch.

- **git pull**: This command fetches and integrates changes from a remote repository into your local repository. It updates your local branch with the latest changes from the remote branch. For example, `git pull origin main` fetches and merges changes from the remote main branch into your local main branch.


I learned the following Quarto commands:

- **quarto preview**: This command starts a local web server and opens a preview of your Quarto project in your default web browser. It allows you to see how your website will look before publishing it. For example, running `quarto preview` in the terminal will generate a live preview of your site.


I learned the following markdown syntax:

- **Headers**: Use `#` for headers. The number of `#` symbols indicates the level of the header. For example, `# Header 1`, `## Header 2`, and `### Header 3`.

- **Bold text**: Use `**` or `__` to make text bold. For example, `**bold**` or `__bold__` will render as bold.

- **Italic text**: Use `*` or `_` to make text italic. For example, `*italic*` or `_italic_` will render as italic.
